fields.title: Handling forms
fields.description: A contact form in a brick: a plain form post, a server handler that emails it, and the result on the page, without JavaScript.

data.title: Keep the recipient on the server
data.body: Don't make the recipient a brick field the form sends along: anyone could post their own address and use your site to send mail. The example reads it from `CONTACT_TO`. Fields the server needs, like a subject or a list to sign up to, can be brick fields shown in the form, but treat whatever the post contains as untrusted.

data.source:
## Spam and abuse

The example keeps it simple:

- A hidden honeypot field. People never see it, so a value in it means a bot. The handler answers "sent" and sends nothing, so the bot doesn't learn to skip it.
- A per-client limit with `createLimiter`, the same counter `createMiddleware` uses for sign-in attempts. It keys on `X-Forwarded-For`, which only a proxy in front of the server sets reliably; without one, pass your own key or rely on the honeypot.
- A cap on the body size and on each field's length.

For a busy site, add a CAPTCHA (Turnstile, hCaptcha) to the form and verify its token in the handler.

## With JavaScript

The same handler serves a form that hydrates later (an island, say): post the form with `fetch` and `redirect: 'manual'`, or give the handler a JSON answer when the request asks for one. Starting from the plain form means the page still works when scripts don't load.
